findings.quote: Because natural views tend to produce positive responses, they may be more effective in reducing stress, decreasing anxiety, holding attention, and improving mood.

findings.consequent: Proper functioning of internal body systems (nervous, endocrine, circadian rhythms, pituitary, pineal gland)
findings.quote: Wavelengths of light help control the human body's chemistry.

findings.consequent: Vitamin D synthesis, prevention/cure of rickets and osteomalacia
findings.quote: Sunlight striking the skin initiated a series of reactions in the body leading to the production of vitamin D, a necessary ingredient for the absorption of calcium and other minerals from the diet.

findings.antecedent: Lack of proper light (especially in winter/higher latitudes)
findings.quote: Without the proper amount of light available, our circadian rhythms are affected and susceptibility to SAD is increased.
Appropriate administration of light therapy clears the symptoms within a few days.

School children and teachers can benefit from integrating and managing daylight properly. Reported benefits include reduced utility costs for school districts, improved student attendance and academic performance, and a less stressful environment for students.

findings.consequent: Higher reading and math achievement scores / faster learning rates
findings.quote: Students in the daylit schools had higher reading and math achievement scores.

Substantiating the claim of increased sales, the chief architect of Southern California Edison, Gregg D. Ander, applied daylighting to stores for the largest retailer in the country and possibly the world. Ander said this retail chain has had successful sales for the daylit stores when compared to the nondaylit stores in the district.

findings.consequent: Improved patient recovery rates / shorter hospital stays
findings.quote: Studies show that daylit post-surgical facilities improve this mental well-being. Intensive Care Unit (ICU) areas in hospitals can be very stressful for patients and workers (Collins 1975).

findings.antecedent: Improper daylighting (high lighting levels, excessive glare, high temperatures)
findings.consequent: Reduced productivity, increased absenteeism, discomfort, dissatisfaction, eye fatigue
findings.quote: Improper use of daylighting can reduce productivity and increase employee absenteeism due to the possibility of extremely high lighting levels, excessive glare, and high temperatures.

findings.consequent: Negative psychological effects (claustrophobia, unhappiness, depression, isolation, tension), physical ailments (headaches, sickness, fatigue), decreased job satisfaction, increased vandalism
findings.quote: The specific reasons given for the dislike of the windowless offices were: 'no daylight, poor ventilation, inability to know about the weather, inability to see out and have a view, feelings of being cooped-up, feelings of isolation and claustrophobia, and feelings of depression and tension.'
